summary: The team is juggling urgent IT access fixes, a knowledge website redesign, and a major marketing pivot to prioritize Asia Star and Intelligent China while pausing US partnerships.
summaryDetail: Right now, the most immediate issue is an Outlook account lockout that requires deleting the old account and re-logging in with a new password on all devices, plus contacting JSB to confirm backend unlock. In parallel, the Knowledge Website Redesign is moving forward: combine the current design with Joseph's version, remove the videos panel, keep the two top menus, and incorporate BCI/BSI indices; Joseph must share the HTML file and huddle with Julie and the speaker for specific feedback before Joker implements changes. On the marketing front, the team has decided to prioritize Asia Star and Intelligent China for SEO and marketing, put US partnerships on hold for Q1 (with Berkeley as a third priority), and is auditing conversion tracking while Joseph requests a detailed brief from the SEO team. Upcoming deadlines include the Investor Sentiment Survey report and press release edits by noon today, the September newsletter review, and the 2026 WIL Forum agenda feedback and UN Women China follow-up by September 17.

decisions.text: Remove the videos panel and disperse videos by topic instead of having a separate category.
Keep the two menus (knowledge and school) at the top, with the school menu at the top right in gray and the knowledge menu centered.
Incorporate BCI and BSI indices into the knowledge section, similar to the school homepage.
Combine elements from the current design and Joseph's version, showing more articles and bringing indices to the front.
Prioritize Asia Star and Intelligent China programs for marketing efforts.
Put US partnerships on hold for the first quarter, but consider Berkeley as a third priority.
The internal linking system is now live on the Knowledge website, with 86.5% of articles carrying internal links.
